claims.claim: For a German student visa applied for in India, an APS certificate is always mandatory unless an exception applies.
You do not need an APS certificate if you will obtain a non-German degree in Germany.
You do not need an APS certificate if you will do PhD/postdoc studies.
You do not need an APS certificate if you received a scholarship from German or EU public funds.
You do not need an APS certificate if your studies build on a non-Indian school certificate (e.g. International Baccalaureate) or a non-Indian degree (e.g. a British Bachelor).
Bachelor/master applicants requiring APS, scholarship holders and PhD/postdoc applicants apply at VFS.
Those studying for non-German degrees apply at the Embassy or a Consulate.
Booking an appointment in the wrong category means your application won't be accepted.
Universities may set their own APS rules.
Applicants with an Indian school or university degree must have their certificates checked by APS in New Delhi.
The visa checklist is dated September 2024.

reference_key_facts: Yes, APS certificate is mandatory for Indian applicants for a German student visa
Exceptions exist: obtaining a non-German degree in Germany
correctness.explanation: The assistant says the APS certificate is mandatory and lists all the reference's exceptions: a non-German degree, PhD/postdoc studies, and scholarships. It adds further details but contradicts nothing in the reference.

claims.claim: Most international students use a blocked account called a 'Sperrkonto' as proof of sufficient funds.
With a Sperrkonto, the money is shown as a credit to the account.
A Sperrkonto may only allow a certain level of withdrawals each month.
A Sperrkonto can only be closed with approval from an embassy, consulate or the competent foreigners authority.
The German embassy in India currently requires €11,904 in a blocked account for the first year of studies.
No more than €992 per month can be withdrawn from the blocked account.
A formal obligation letter ('Verpflichtungserklärung') from a sponsor living in Germany is an alternative proof of funds.
Proof of a German/EU scholarship is an alternative proof of funds.
Sperrkonten are available from several providers.
The best approach is to get advice from the German embassy or consulate.

reference_key_facts: Most international students use a blocked account (Sperrkonto) as proof of funds
correctness.explanation: The assistant says most students use a blocked account (Sperrkonto) as proof of funds. Its extra details (€11,904 per year, €992 per month, and the alternatives) do not contradict the reference.
